judge: Claude Code subagent, Claude Opus 5.5, fresh

items.label: A
items.critique: Mannered, slightly arch shopkeeper voice ('I surmise', 'sorry band of thieves', 'lose no sleep fretting about his soul') with the gold amount spelled out in the thanks; that is Westwood's register.

items.label: B
items.critique: The first ask is one breathless run-on sentence of chained 'and's that no Westwood NPC speaks; the second ask and both outcomes are clipped to near-telegram length, so the lengths swing wildly.

items.label: C
items.critique: Plain, functional exchange with a yes/no branch, an odd specific errand (apples, urchin, aggravated bats) and an item handed over by name ('ruby key'); this is the campaign's sponsorship quest in shape and tone.

items.label: D
items.critique: Excited, exclamation-heavy plea with stock thanks ('token of my appreciation'), a mild comic stake (the father's cloak) and a loose comma splice; reads like Westwood's quick villager quests.

items.label: E
items.critique: Comic touches ('the menfolk cannot live without us', the Ogres' stomachs grumbling) set in a dialogue tree with an accept/decline branch and a reminder line; it reads as authentic Nox.

items.label: F
items.critique: Short, tidy sentences with an assembled feel ('tithe chest', 'I'll see you right', 'hardly a scratch on it'); a too-neat chain to the next quest ('go see [Person]'), and the rewards are generic arms without Westwood's flourish.

items.label: G
items.critique: Casual, dialect-tinged humour ('Oh, bah!', 'ya', running a smuggling ring is hard) and a key with a practical warning about the wizards; very Westwood.

items.label: H
items.critique: The headmaster's speech is close to Nox but stacks fragments for effect ('on the floor, among the books!'), and the dueling-yard ask is a terse vignette whose outcome is a bare quip; it reads like a pastiche.

items.label: I
items.critique: It opens in the middle of a story ('...and I ran!'), the wanted-poster joke is self-consciously writerly ('It looks more like a fish. I can't draw.') and the dead/alive pricing is stated too mechanically; the outcomes are short and blunt.

items.label: J
items.critique: Another long run-on sentence of chained 'and's in the first ask, the pompous warden's 'darkest hour' formula, and a petition subplot that repeats B's 'sign this paper' device; the voices are overwritten and their lengths uneven.

tells: Generated asks often hold one huge run-on sentence chained with 'and' to sound breathless; Westwood keeps its sentences short even in panic and splits them with ' / ' page breaks.

Generated outcomes are clipped to one or two exclamations ('Here, take the boots.'); Westwood's thanks usually name the gold amount in a set phrase ('Here's your reward -- 250 in gold!') or add a warning or a joke.

Generated texts reuse devices across quests (petitions to sign, 'put in a good word', staffs and shields as rewards); Westwood's errands are odder and more specific (apples and an urchin, a father's cloak, a smuggling shipment).

Westwood's humour is folksy and comes from the situation (hungry Ogres, menfolk who cannot cope, a boss who gets arrested to dodge work); generated humour is writerly and self-aware (a badly drawn poster, 'may he choke on his supper').
Westwood often builds quests as dialogue trees with accept and decline branches and reminder lines; generated pairs tend to be two independent asks each followed by its own completion line.
